correctness.rationale: All graph vertices, metric scales and integer thresholds are explicitly defined. The scale-two 56-step collapse is relative to the original graph, proving the persistent first-homology isomorphism. At scale three, 847 faces have an explicit 399-pair discrete-Morse matching; the complete 3010-incidence directed Hasse graph is acyclic and only one vertex plus forty-eight two-cells remain, proving the wedge of spheres. At scale four a contractible-two-piece union with intersection B_P*B_L, where each B collapses to a rank-eight graph, proves a wedge of sixty-four four-spheres; a 3927-pair acyclic Morse witness and mod-two boundaries independently corroborate this. At scale five each edge-centered closed two-neighborhood union is all fourteen vertices. The full reduced integral barcode follows by homotopy and inter-scale maps. The actual packaged verify.py was executed and returned VERIFY_OK; checks are exhaustive for this fixed graph and not used to justify broader families.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the smallest cubic girth-six graph, so scale three is the first threshold outside the established graph-recovery range. The complete barcode at this natural obstruction boundary features non-obvious 48 sphere classes in dimension two and then 64 in dimension four; an independent structural join decomposition explains the second jump. A full integral homotopy-and-persistence classification for this canonical graph has intrinsic topological significance and can serve as a finite benchmark for graph Čech theory. It is not a routine normalization or an arbitrary parameter slice.
